criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5.2 replaces Customer ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations with a license construct. Vendor retains ownership, while Customer receives an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license covering fine-tuned adapter weights, adapter layers, LoRA matrices, and related model parameters.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5.2 includes a broad worldwide covenant by Vendor not to assert any patent, copyright, trade secret, trademark, or other intellectual property right against Customer’s post-termination use, deployment, modification, or further development of the exported Customer-Trained Adaptations, binding Vendor and its successors and assigns.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to provide an API-based export of the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, within 30 days after termination or expiration and in an industry-standard format such as ONNX, SafeTensors, or a mutually agreed equivalent. Section 13.6(g) reinforces the same requirement.

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a dedicated Technology Escrow article and Exhibit E covering deposit of fine-tuned adapter weights, related configuration/pipeline artifacts, release triggers, verification, and a post-release perpetual license. These provisions expressly support the perpetual-license construct for Customer-Trained Adaptations in Section 5.2.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 sets the general aggregate liability cap at one and one-half times (1.5×) the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly equal to $3,600,000.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 establishes a Super-Cap of three times the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly equal to $7,200,000, and applies it to Vendor liability for Article 6 data-processing/data-breach matters and indemnification obligations under Sections 11.1 and 11.2, including IP indemnity.

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 expressly states that liability arising from either party’s willful misconduct or gross negligence “shall remain fully uncapped,” excluding it from both the General Cap and Super-Cap. The updated issues list also consistently confirms this treatment.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act solely as a CCPA service provider/processor, not an independent controller, in Section 6.2. Exhibit D also includes Vendor’s service-provider certification and cites Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag).

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly prohibits use of Customer Data, including de-identified or aggregated derivatives, for model improvement or training unless the data meets the CCPA de-identification standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and is independently verified in writing by a third-party assessor approved in writing by TechNova before use. DPA Section 3A also expressly states that this is a specific contractual obligation.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the Platform availability requirement at 99.95% for each calendar month in Section 9.1, and Exhibit B reflects the same monthly uptime target.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly excludes scheduled maintenance windows and Force Majeure Events from Downtime in Section 9.1, subject to specified maintenance notice and duration limits. Exhibit B also repeats both exclusions.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the API latency SLA at the ninety-fifth percentile to p95 ≤ 450 ms in Section 9.2 and consistently reflects that threshold in Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list identifies the 450 ms p95 latency SLA as a “Yellow-zone concession” and expressly notes that Product/Engineering still strongly prefers sub-400 ms latency for LendStream real-time decisioning.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the initial model accuracy threshold at F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day Stabilization Period and at Go-Live, including in Section 9.3, Exhibit A, and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contractually sets F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day Stabilization Period following the October 1, 2025 Go-Live and increases the target to F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026. This ramp is reflected in Section 9.3 and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly caps aggregate SLA Service Credits at 20% of the $200,000 monthly Annual Platform Fee installment, equal to $40,000 per month, in Section 9.4 and Exhibit B Section 5(c).

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 retains Section 9.5, allowing Customer to terminate on 30 days’ written notice if Vendor misses any SLA target for three or more consecutive calendar months. Exhibit B also repeats this trigger.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 inserts a new Section 11.2, “Vendor AI-Output Indemnification,” requiring Vendor to defend, indemnify, and hold Customer harmless from third-party claims alleging that AI-generated Platform outputs infringe or misappropriate third-party intellectual property rights or violate applicable law.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.2 expressly excludes AI-Output Claims to the extent caused by Customer’s modification of an output after receipt or Customer’s use of the Platform outside the documented use case in the applicable SOW.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.1 expressly broadens Vendor’s IP indemnity to all Intellectual Property Rights worldwide arising from Customer’s authorized use, including registered and unregistered patents and copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, moral rights, publicity rights, database rights, and analogous foreign rights. It is not limited to registered U.S. patents and copyrights.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires escrow of all fine-tuned adapter weights and all training configuration and pipeline artifacts necessary to render, reproduce, or redeploy those weights. It expressly excludes Base Model source code, Base Model weights, and Vendor’s proprietary training infrastructure.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 identifies Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the proposed Escrow Agent, and the updated issues list expressly identifies NCC Group plc as the fallback escrow agent.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes all three required escrow release triggers in Section 5A.3: Vendor insolvency, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 days after notice, and Vendor cessation of product support for the MeridianIQ Platform.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets Technology Errors & Omissions / Cyber Liability Insurance at $5,000,000 per occurrence, accepting Meridian's current policy limit.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly identifies Tech E&O at $5 million per occurrence as a “Yellow-zone item” and states that, because TCV is $7.2 million, the playbook prefers $10 million, with $5 million as the absolute minimum.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 maintains Delaware governing law in Section 14.1, which states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. No other state's law is specified as governing law.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.2 specifies exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, where subject-matter jurisdiction exists, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, and does not require arbitration.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 3 expressly certifies that Vendor is a “service provider” as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and restricts Vendor from selling, sharing, or retaining Customer Data except as necessary to perform under the Agreement. The agreement also incorporates the DPA and references this certification in Sections 6.2 and 6.8.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. Exhibit D, Section 4 states that Vendor acknowledges Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to GLBA and agrees to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements. Sections 6.3 and 6.4 also reference GLBA, the FTC Safeguards Rule, and required security controls.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a 72-hour breach-notification deadline in Exhibit D, Section 8, requiring Vendor to notify Customer without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after discovery or awareness of an actual or reasonably suspected Security Breach.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Customer’s prior written consent before Vendor may engage any sub-processor, both in Section 6.6 of the Agreement and Section 6 of the DPA.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 3A requires de-identification that satisfies the CCPA statutory standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), including safeguards against re-identification, and requires written verification by an independent third-party assessor approved by Customer before use.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses post-termination data return/deletion. Section 10 of Exhibit D requires Vendor to return or delete all Customer Data within 30 days of Customer’s written request and certify completion, incorporating Section 6.7 of the Agreement, which provides detailed return/deletion obligations upon termination or expiration.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/licensing, liability cap, data processing/de-identification, uptime, latency, accuracy/F1, SLA credits, escrow, AI-output indemnity, IP indemnity scope, Tech E&O insurance, and governing law/dispute resolution.

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 5, “IP ownership / license structure,” as “Partially Resolved” and explains that the perpetual-license construct is a fallback subject to material protective conditions, consistent with Meridian not yet agreeing to the full package.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the general liability cap (item 6) as "Open," reflecting that Draft 3 proposes a 1.5× compromise while Meridian has not accepted it. This satisfies the criterion, which permits either "Partially Resolved" or "Open."

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 8, “Data processing / CCPA service-provider,” as “Partially Resolved” and explains that service-provider status is mandatory while the de-identification and independent-verification conditions remain to be raised on the joint call.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the Uptime SLA as “Resolved” at 99.95% monthly, with agreed exclusions for scheduled maintenance and Force Majeure events.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the latency SLA as “Partially Resolved,” states that Draft 3 accepts p95 latency of 450 ms, and notes that Product/Engineering still strongly prefers sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning.

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the Accuracy/F1 SLA as "Open" and states that Draft 3 proposes F1 ≥ 0.92 during stabilization, ramping to F1 ≥ 0.94 from January 1, 2026, which Meridian has not yet accepted.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes SLA credits as “Open,” noting that the proposed 20% monthly cap has not been accepted by Meridian. This satisfies the criterion, which permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open.”

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes escrow (item 13) as “Open,” reflecting that the agent and scope remain disputed. The criterion expressly accepts either “Partially Resolved” or “Open” and only fails if escrow is marked fully “Resolved.”

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 9, “AI-output indemnity,” as “Open” and notes that Meridian has not provided a substantive response.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 10, “IP indemnity scope,” as “Open” and notes that the broadened all-IP coverage has been proposed but remains under negotiation.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 11, “Insurance / Tech E&O,” as “Partially Resolved” and expressly flags it as a “Yellow-zone item.”

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 12, governing law/dispute resolution, as “Open” and notes that there has been no movement, with Meridian continuing to prefer Massachusetts law and AAA Boston arbitration.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly states that its new tracked changes are shown against the clean, accepted Draft 2 base, and the document contains insertion and deletion markup reflecting those changes. The updated issues list likewise confirms that Draft 3 is tracked against the accepted Draft 2 base.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per Contract Year in Section 4.1, with monthly installments of $200,000. The updated issues list also confirms the $2.4 million annual fee as resolved and unchanged.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the three-year Initial Term. Section 13.1 states that it begins on July 1, 2025 and expires on June 30, 2028, consistent with the defined Initial Term and the updated issues list.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the one-time implementation fee at $850,000 and splits it into two equal $425,000 installments: the first upon execution of the Initial SOW and the second upon Go-Live. Exhibit A confirms the same milestone payment schedule.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves 40,000,000 included API calls per Contract Year and an overage rate of $0.012 per API call in Section 4.3; the updated issues list also confirms these terms.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.2 preserves automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives at least 180 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal. The updated issues list also confirms the 180-day notice period as resolved.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies 450 ms as a Playbook Yellow-range concession, notes Product/Engineering’s preference for sub-400 ms, and ties that preference to LendStream real-time decisioning. This provides the required acceptable-range-versus-preferred-target context.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The latency issue is marked partially resolved, notes that Product/Engineering still prefers sub-400 ms, expressly recommends revisiting it on the joint call, and includes latency on the joint-call agenda.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list identifies AI-output indemnity as item 9, marks it “Open,” and expressly states that “Meridian has not provided a substantive response.” This satisfies the criterion that the issue remain fully open and Meridian’s lack of substantive response be noted.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly states for item 9, AI-output indemnity: “Playbook fallback: shared-risk framework with Meridian first-dollar coverage up to the applicable cap or super-cap.” This satisfies the required fallback position.
